project.objective: Present realistic service work through the user-selected mix of process scenes with people or hands and detailed object-led service imagery.
project.governing_idea: The work and the process share the spotlight.

creative_system.visual_thesis: Realistic commercial imagery balances selected creative-process scenes with tangible outputs, equipment and product still lifes.
anti_goals: Generic portraits disconnected from the service
Implausible anatomy, disconnected people or equipment

creative_system.lighting: Plausible window or practical studio light.
creative_system.typography: Service labels and descriptions remain live HTML. Incidental illustrative interfaces use minimal copy.
creative_system.interface: Clear hierarchy, responsive reflow, keyboard access, and reduced-motion parity.
invariants: Use the user-selected mixed direction: six process/reference scenes that may include people or hands, and six object-led scenes.

permitted_variations: People or hands in strategy, brand, campaigns, search, commerce and production references.

shots.action: Create a high-end commercial photograph for a creative agency service page. The subject is the service's tangible work, never a person. Photographic realism: physically plausible materials, small surface imperfections, coherent perspective and contact shadows, restrained color grading, natural optical depth. The main subject must remain recognizable in a centered near-square crop, while the full image is composed beautifully. No people, body parts, hands, faces, silhouettes, human reflections, portraits, mannequins, humanoid robots, or human figures in printed artwork or on screens. No floating objects, holograms, fantasy interfaces, visualized glowing networks, exaggerated CGI polish, watermarks, fake endorsements, performance claims or tiny invented text. An exceptionally beautiful finished editorial coffee product still life photographed for a brand's content campaign. A glazed ivory ceramic espresso cup with a rich coffee crema sits on a small pale travertine plinth; beside it a plain folded cocoa-brown paper coffee pouch, two scattered coffee beans and a casually folded oatmeal linen napkin. A sliver of the saucer and deep chestnut shadows add depth. No text or labels on the pouch. Low warm morning window light rakes the real ceramic glaze, tiny coffee bubbles, paper seams and natural linen fibres. The cup is the dominant subject, not production equipment. Tasteful, rich, tactile, photorealistic, 85mm product photograph.
